justification: Both surfaces show the same specific repertoire: a profile human hand with carefully separated fingers gripping a small object, richly fringed and tasselled robe edges rendered as rows of tight repeated strokes, and rosette/floral motifs set in bands beside the figure, all in an identically fine, low-relief incised convention. The main difference in depicted content is that A is only a fragment dominated by a broad register of dense repeated sign-like marks across the surface, with no complete figure, whereas B shows a whole winged, bearded standing figure with one arm raised, so the overall composition can only be inferred rather than matched.
